por_que: It is what you do today: the baseline to compare the other options.
With your weather, on average you lose 0.1 of every 10 seasons (grain < 70% of normal).

estrategias.descripcion: Sorghum in Primera and beans relay-planted when the maize is doubled over; half of the residue stays on the soil.

por_que: Uses the Postrera rains (from Aug 10) with beans: if Primera fails, there is still a harvest.
Cuts lost seasons from 0.1 to 0.0 of every 10.
evidencia: Daily FAO-56 water balance with the real weather of 25 seasons (NASA POWER 2001–2025): typical canícula from Jul 12 to Aug 1.
Monte Carlo of 1000 sequences of 10 seasons, with uncertain planting date and soil water.
Postrera onset computed year by year with the Sivakumar (1988) rule; Postrera beans: 12 qq/mz typical.
Relay beans or sorghum in Postrera is common practice in eastern Guatemala (MAGA; FAO Dry Corridor).
beneficios: More food: 36 qq/mz in total (range 34–37) and a second harvest to sell.
Less bare soil: 147 fewer days a year; erosion ≈ 49 t/ha/yr less.
Beans fix nitrogen and break maize pest cycles.
info_faltante: Local price of beans or sorghum and access to seed.
Whether your land holds moisture in September (very thin soils dry fast).
riesgos: Dry Postrera in El Niño years: with El Niño, sorghum is safer than beans.
More work in September, right when you double the maize.
Bean pests and diseases in heavy rain: check with the extension agent.

estrategias.descripcion: Sorghum in Primera and velvet bean (mucuna) planted ~50 days later; no burning: the cover and residue protect the soil all year.

por_que: The velvet bean (mucuna) covers the soil almost all year: less evaporation and more water soaking in (runoff 30 → 11 mm).
It protects the soil the most: erosion ≈ 4 t/ha/yr (vs 61 today) and organic matter -0.26 points in 5 years.
evidencia: Daily FAO-56 water balance with the real weather of 25 seasons (NASA POWER 2001–2025): typical canícula from Jul 12 to Aug 1.
Monte Carlo of 1000 sequences of 10 seasons, with uncertain planting date and soil water.
Velvet-bean green-manure systems on hillsides of Honduras and Guatemala (Buckles et al. 1998, CIMMYT/IDRC; Bunch 2003).
Mulch effect on evaporation per FAO-56 ch. 7; erosion with RUSLE (Renard et al. 1997).
beneficios: Fixes nitrogen: maize yield can rise over the years (up to +15%, approx.); typical harvest 26 qq/mz.
Bare soil: only ~11 days a year (vs 262 today).
Fewer weeds and no burning needed.
info_faltante: Where to get velvet bean (mucuna) seed and how much.
How much biomass the cover reaches on your land (we estimate it with the water balance).
Whether free-roaming livestock will eat the cover in the dry season.
riesgos: Competes with maize for water if planted too early: sow it after the first weeding.
Velvet bean seed is not edible without processing (it contains L-dopa).
Soil benefits take 2–3 years to show; try it on a small plot first.

incertidumbre: Data for a ~50 km zone (not your exact plot). Ranges go from the 10% to the 90% of 10000 simulated seasons. Yield can vary ±30–50%: compare options, we do not promise quintales. In El Niño years ([2002 2004 2009 2015 2023]) today you lose 0.4 of every 10 seasons; in other years, 0.0. El Niño is active now (ONI 2.5, ASO 2026).

ia_vs_estadistica.nota: AI: logistic regression on 4 inputs known at planting (ONI AMJ, rain Apr 15–May 31 (z), root-zone wetness GWETROOT May (z), Tmax Apr–May (z)) trained on 825 seasons (33 NASA POWER zones × 2001–2025). Statistics: loss frequency by zone and El Niño state. Leave-one-year-out validation: Brier error AI 0.154 vs statistics 0.161 (lower is better) → here the AI model wins. Probability of losing next Primera if El Niño persists at planting: both are shown; the engine uses statistics.

confianza.habilidad: acertó la temporada en 14 de 25 años (56 % vs 33 % al azar) · pérdida: Brier 0.260 vs 0.236 · detectó 4 de 8 sequías documentadas · Brier IA 0.154 vs estadística 0.161
confianza.texto: Los primeros 16 días son el pronóstico; el resto repite 2005, el año más representativo de los parecidos al pronóstico estacional (ECMWF SEAS5) y a El Niño pronosticado. Para la milpa de siempre se espera una temporada regular (54 % de probabilidad; en 11 de 24 años pasó algo así). Con esta estrategia: cosecha probable 37–37 qq/mz, riesgo de perderla 0 %. Confianza media.
confianza.texto_en: The first 16 days are the forecast; the rest replays 2005, the most representative year among those resembling the seasonal forecast (ECMWF SEAS5) and the forecast El Niño. For the usual milpa, expect a fair season (54% probability; it happened in 11 of 24 years). With this strategy: likely harvest 37–37 qq/mz, 0% risk of losing it. Confidence medium.

confianza.regla: Puntos: probabilidad del escenario ≥ 60 % → 2 (≥ 40 % → 1); validación local con ≥ 60 % de sequías documentadas detectadas → 1; temporada armada con pronóstico (o clima observado) → 1; rango de cosecha estrecho ((P90−P10)/P50 ≤ 0.5) → 1. alta ≥ 4, media 2–3, baja ≤ 1. Clima observado = alta; escenarios CMIP6 a 2040 como máximo media; nunca por encima del nivel medido en el hindcast 2001–2025 del lugar (static/validacion/habilidad.json).

siembra.texto: Sembrá el 20 may y cosechás cerca del 26 sep (129 días). Es la fecha con menos riesgo de la ventana: pérdida 0 de cada 10 temporadas parecidas, cosecha típica 37 qq/mz.
siembra.texto_en: Sow on May 20 and harvest around Sep 26 (129 days). It is the lowest-risk date in the window: loss in 0 of 10 similar seasons, typical harvest 37 qq/mz.

razones.texto: Lluvia en la cosecha (cerca del 26 sep): 155 mm en promedio; en 5 de cada 10 años más de 150 mm (mazorca que se pudre, secado difícil).
razones.texto_en: Rain at harvest (around Sep 26): 155 mm on average; in 5 of 10 years over 150 mm (ear rot, hard drying).

razones.texto: Falso inicio: en 3 de cada 10 años parecidos vino una racha de 7+ días secos en el primer mes después de sembrar el 20 may (la semilla nace y se seca).
razones.texto_en: False start: in 3 of 10 similar years a 7+ day dry spell came in the first month after sowing on May 20 (seedlings emerge and dry out).
